question: How much of the repaired strict-LOSO B1 continuous error can be removed by GT-assisted bounded temporal shifts?
protocol: MMECG loso_v2 folds 1/5/9 development validation only; test unopened
preprocessing: Fourth-order zero-phase Butterworth 0.5-40 Hz applied independently to prediction and target, followed by per-window z-scoring
correlation_rule: For every window and tolerance, maximize PCC over integer lags within the tolerance. All lags use the same samples 20:1580 of the target and a shifted 1560-sample prediction support, so support length never changes with lag.
aggregation: Window PCC first; mean within fold; then equal-weight fold-macro mean across folds. Per-window best lags at +/-100 ms are retained.
required_outputs: raw unfiltered full-window PCC@0 for continuity with the primary metric
filtered fixed-support NCC curve per fold and fold-macro
JSON and CSV artifacts plus publication-style PNG/PDF
interpretation_guard: Max-lag NCC consumes validation ECG and is an oracle diagnostic, never deployable performance. A rise localizes timing sensitivity but does not by itself prove physiological EMAT or identify a radar-only correction.
test_policy: Validation only. The script rejects any split other than val.
